subject: Converting flat-fee private offer to usage billing + reseller crediting
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@healthgrid.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alexa Perez <alexa.perez@cloudbridge.io>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Converting private offer: flat-fee to usage-based + channel crediting

Hey Ben —

Quick context: HealthGrid is currently on a flat private offer with Redwood (monthly billed, fixed $120k/mo). Our reseller CloudBridge (Alexa cc'd) was paid a 12% commission on the historical list/commit. We're evaluating moving to a usage-based model (metered) for the next contract term, but procurement needs clarity on how the existing channel passback/commission will be honored and how the marketplace invoice will look.

Specific asks:
- Two practical options for converting the existing flat-fee commitment to usage pricing, including an illustrative invoice/credit example.
- How we keep CloudBridge's economic position intact (do we do an explicit reseller credit, list-price anchoring, or something else?).
- Whether Redwood can do retroactive credits for Jan if we close amendment this month.
- Any impacts to tax/invoicing and PO handling.

Attaching our PO stub and current monthly usage exports — will share anything else you need. Can we do a call tomorrow morning PST?

Thanks,
Samir Khan
VP, Cloud Ops
HealthGrid
attachments: HealthGrid_PO_2027.pdf (PO stub), usage-report-jan.csv (referenced)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Converting private offer: flat-fee to usage-based + channel crediting

Samir — thanks for the clear ask. High-level we can do this two ways (I've summarized with pros/cons and next steps):

Option A — List-price conversion + reseller credit (recommended for speed)
- We convert the existing flat-fee to an equivalent usage SKU by anchoring the list price to the implied per-unit rate from your current $120k/month.
- Redwood issues invoices via the marketplace SKU; CloudBridge receives the normal marketplace commission. Redwood will issue a one-time reseller credit to CloudBridge to preserve the delta to their target 12% net.
- Pros: preserves marketplace invoicing, minimal catalog churn, quick to implement.
- Cons: needs a one-time finance credit and simple amendment.

Option B — New usage SKU + explicit passback (cleaner long-term)
- Create a new metered SKU on marketplace. Redwood invoices usage; we run a separate commission passback to CloudBridge on invoiced gross revenue (explicit credit line item).
- Pros: clear accounting for future usage, easier for long-term telemetry.
- Cons: requires ops to onboard new SKU and mapping; slightly longer lead time.

Examples and numbers: I attached a short PDF with two worked examples (conversion-scenarios.pdf). We need three inputs from your side to finalize numbers: current monthly average usage, desired reseller net % (you mentioned 12%), and whether you want a list-price floor for the first 6 months.

On retro credits: finance will consider up to 3 months retroactive credit (subject to signed amendment & PO). I'll loop in Marcus and Naomi to confirm policy and expected timing.

Available for a call tomorrow 9:30–11:00am PST. If that works, I can send a calendar invite with a short mutual action plan.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference
attachments: pricing-conversion-scenarios.pdf

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@healthgrid.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alexa Perez <alexa.perez@cloudbridge.io>, procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Converting flat-fee private offer: flat-fee to usage-based + channel crediting

Thanks Ben — helpful framing. A few data points to plug into your examples:
- Current committed amount: $120,000 / month (flat private offer).
- CloudBridge commission target: 12% of what they historically received.
- We expect usage to be lumpy in Q2, but a 10–15% QoQ growth profile for the first 6 months.

Questions:
- If we choose Option A (list-price conversion + reseller credit), does the reseller credit land on the marketplace invoice (so CloudBridge sees it on their statement) or is it handled as a separate vendor credit to be paid out later? We prefer the former for invoice transparency.
- Can you provide a worked example showing: (1) gross invoice to HealthGrid, (2) marketplace commission, (3) reseller credit that nets CloudBridge to the 12% they expect.
- On retro credits: we would like Jan included if possible. If Redwood can commit to Jan + Feb credits (capped to 3 months), we can expedite the amendment and send a signed PO.

I'll attach a quick spreadsheet with monthly totals — thank you for looping Marcus and Naomi.

—Samir
attachments: healthgrid-breakdown.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Converting flat-fee private offer: flat-fee to usage-based + channel crediting

Samir — attaching the detailed workbook with sample math (healthgrid-breakdown.xlsx). Key points from the models:

- If we anchor list-price to implied per-unit rate from $120k/mo and estimate first-month usage at the current run rate, here's a simplified line example:
  * Gross invoice (marketplace): $120,000
  * Marketplace commission (example 5% listing fee): $6,000
  * Gross revenue credited to CloudBridge (12% target): $14,400
  * One-time reseller credit to CloudBridge to make them whole: $8,400 (difference between marketplace commission and their target)
  * Net owed by HealthGrid remains $120,000 — the credit is between Redwood and CloudBridge.

- We can render the reseller credit as a distinct line on the CloudBridge statement; it will not alter the customer-facing invoice. That gives Alexa visibility and keeps your accounts payable flow unchanged.

- Retro credit: finance confirms we can do up to 3 months retro back-dated, conditional on: signed amendment, PO referencing the amendment, and CloudBridge sending their commission statement for reconciliation. Marcus — can we confirm this as a policy?

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm you want Option A or B.
2) Sign a brief amendment (we'll draft).
3) We process 1–3 months retro credits (if you elect).
4) Transition billing to the usage SKU with a 6-month ramp and a list-price floor (we recommend 80% of implied list for the first 6 months).

I'm sending a calendar invite for a quick 30-min sync at 11:00am PST.

Cheers,
Ben
attachments: healthgrid-breakdown.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Converting flat-fee private offer: flat-fee to usage-based + channel crediting

Quick internal: finance is comfortable approving retro credits up to 3 months (Jan–Mar window) provided the following are met:
- Signed amendment attached to incoming PO
- CloudBridge provides a commission statement for reconciliation within 30 days of amendment
- Credits will be processed as vendor credits to CloudBridge and shown as a distinct line on their statement (not customer invoice).

Laura — please coordinate the credit memo flow and confirm the expected processing SLA (we typically do 30–45 days after amendment).

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@healthgrid.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alexa Perez <alexa.perez@cloudbridge.io>, procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 15:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Converting flat-fee private offer: flat-fee to usage-based + channel crediting

Ben/Marcus — this is great, thank you. We will proceed with Option A and request Jan+Feb retro credits (2 months). Alexa will email CloudBridge's commission statement tonight. Procurement will send the signed amendment + updated PO by end of day Monday.

Please treat this as priority — we'd like billing flipped to the usage SKU starting Mar 1 with a 6-month ramp and the 80% list-price floor you recommended.

Samir Khan
VP, Cloud Ops
HealthGrid
